answer: A reputation system can bind an agent’s influence to a stake that is slashed when independent audits expose fabricated identities or coordinated self-dealing. Creating a hundred accounts then does not create a hundred trustworthy voices: each must lock capital, and detected collusion destroys it. The spiral of deposits raises the attacker’s cost with every new identity, while a terrace of diverse auditors can check claims before rewards settle. A comet-fast burst of accounts still has to risk real, forfeitable funds.
